_status: Module 3, Lesson 3.1, 'Separate rooms: segmentation' (learner guide of 21 October 2026): the zone table and its rule that every connection between zones passes the firewall's rules. The flat network is the 'before'. Fictional office.
title: Separate rooms: a flat network, then zones

steps.title: Everything can reach everything
steps.text: In a flat network there are no internal walls. The firewall guards the internet edge only; inside, every device can talk to every other one.

steps.title: One infected staff PC
steps.text: Malware on one staff computer goes straight for the applicant database. Nothing inside stops it.

verdict.text: One click on one PC exposes every applicant.

steps.title: A visitor's phone, a camera
steps.text: A visitor on the office Wi-Fi opens the file server. A camera with a default password, taken over from outside, reaches the database too.

tracks.label: After: zones that reach only what they need
tracks.desk: Keep personal devices and visitors off the office network.
tracks.it: Zones for guests, devices, staff and servers; every connection passes the firewall.

steps.title: Split the network into zones
steps.text: Each zone reaches only what it needs, and every connection between zones passes the firewall's rules. A problem in one zone cannot reach the others.

steps.title: The infected PC is contained
steps.text: The staff network may reach the portal and the file server, not the database directly.

steps.title: Guests and devices stay in their rooms
steps.text: Guest Wi-Fi reaches the internet only. Cameras and printers reach their own recorder or service only.

steps.title: The work still flows
steps.text: Citizens reach the portal; the portal reaches the database through **one approved connection**; staff reach the file server.

verdict.text: Each zone reaches only what it needs.
